source_context_paragraphs: 16  Scope governance, Agile delivery and FYP handover
M16   ·   MODULE PURPOSE
Keep the team aligned with approved FYP requirements, decisions and university deliverables.
Primary users / surface:  Project team, supervisors, owner, reviewers
Dependencies:  Every module and approved specification/documentation change
Boundary and unresolved details
Proposed extra modules (appointment booking, payments, hospital integrations, doctor chat, prescription writing or admin analytics) require separate owner/supervisor approval.
Module exit demonstration
Complete a requirements/evidence walkthrough and handover demonstration with known limitations clearly identified.
5  Product data model and invariants

These are logical entities required for the product, not a final SQL schema. Implementation identifiers, timestamps and processing state enable approved user features and are not standalone product modules.
5.1  Mandatory data-handling rules
Patient ID is enforced in every ownership and retrieval path; a clinician must also match the selected report IDs on a live grant.
Document date and upload timestamp are distinct. Report-date omissions must not be replaced with invented medical event dates.
Original S3 files, OCR text, embeddings, medical summaries, share grants and guardian email events must remain source-linked.
Deleted/replaced records, historical summaries, email attachments, vector data and backups must follow the separately approved retention/deletion policy (CFG-12).
Only approved synthetic/de-identified material may be used in ordinary development and demonstration; identifiable patient data requires prior authorization.
5.2  Interface responsibilities
6  Non-functional product and engineering requirements

No specific latency, throughput, uptime, OCR score, RAG score, accessibility standard, data-retention duration or recovery target is stated in the submitted proposal. CFG-09 and CFG-10 must define measurable release criteria; this PRD intentionally does not invent numeric promises.
7  Confirmed product and architecture decisions
7.1  Source tensions resolved by confirmed decisions
8  Controlled configuration register (must close before release)

Register policy: Each open configuration requires a named responsible approver, chosen value, justification, timestamp, test case and evidence link. For real-patient use, clinical/privacy approvals and AI-model data handling cannot remain unresolved.
9  Scope boundaries, dependencies and known risks
9.1  Explicit exclusions requiring new approval
Integrated doctor appointment booking/calendar or scheduling
Patient/doctor payment, insurance billing or subscription commerce
Automatic integration/synchronization with hospital or laboratory EHR systems
Doctor-patient instant messaging, telemedicine calls or chat platform
Permanent doctor accounts, clinician CRM and full practice-management dashboards
Guardian login portal or unrestricted guardian record browsing
Medical prescription generation, medication reminders or autonomous treatment recommendations
Independent AI diagnosis, emergency-triage decisions or replacement of licensed clinicians
Public browsing of patient medical records or unrestricted share-by-link
Administrative analytics dashboards, marketing features and unrelated AI tools
Separate patient web portal beyond the selected React Native client
9.2  Product risks and release blockers

known_source_inconsistencies: PRD-M01-06 cites CFG-08 for account/session configuration, but CFG-08 is AWS topology/IAM/network/keys. Preserve the source citation; security/session policy remains explicitly open.
Hosted LLM and Python OCR source allocations conflict with approved local-zero-paid and retained Node OCR development directions. Formal amendments remain pending.
review_policy: Dependency-ordered approved phases; stop after each approved major phase for owner review. Module 01 accepted/PARTIAL and preserved. Do not conduct serial module-only reviews. No automatic B04 or live activation.
